items.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011
items.q: I’d say if every musician would sit down with those Sinatra records and literally copy his phrasing

ctx.x: What about musical, even specifically musical things that you like in other players. Is it possible to put it into words?

Well probably part of it. I would say one of the things I really like is people who can play a melody, render a melody, phrase it with beautiful conversational type phrasing, you know, like a Sinatra phrasing let’s say. I’d say if every musician would sit down with those Sinatra records and literally copy his phrasing, the breathing points and the bigger curve of his phrasing, I think everyone would sound better. You know there’s a lot of concentration on just soloing and the eighth notes and immediately into…
yeah, I look for that, somebody with a sound and a feel and a touch, who can really play a beautiful melody. And of course solo, but, you know.
